description:
About the Position

Wageningen University & Research is recruiting a doctoral researcher to study societal resilience against disaster and war in the Netherlands. The project asks who participates in resilience initiatives, who makes decisions and who benefits. Wageningen University & Research invites applications for a PhD position in this area: Resilience against Disaster and War in the Netherlands at Wageningen, Netherlands. Disciplinary scope: Sociology, Public Policy, Governance. Location: Wageningen, Netherlands. According to the listing, full funding is provided; financial support is listed as €3,204/month. Interested candidates should note the deadline: 2 November 2026.

Research Position Overview

Conduct comparative qualitative fieldwork with municipalities, Safety Regions and other resilience actors. Analyse how government and community initiatives organise participation and distribute responsibilities, working within Sociology of Development and Change. Wageningen University & Research invites applications for a PhD position in this area: Resilience against Disaster and War in the Netherlands at Wageningen, Netherlands. The work sits within Sociology, Public Policy, Governance. The role is based in Wageningen, Netherlands. This is a fully funded opportunity; financial support is listed as €3,204/month. Applications close 2 November 2026.

Research Areas

  • Community resilience
  • Disaster sociology
  • Crisis preparedness

Funding and Duration

Employment and financial support
ComponentDetails
PositionPhD researcher
Salary€3,204–€4,051 gross per month for a 38-hour working week, increasing with doctoral year.
DurationFour years, full-time (38 hours per week): initial 18-month contract, extended subject to satisfactory progress.
Programme / host supportSalaried doctoral employment in the host research group identified in the official vacancy.
Benefits8.3% year-end bonus and pension arrangements; other benefits follow the university employment conditions.

Eligibility and Requirements

Academic preparation and appointment conditions
ComponentDetails
Applicant eligibilityDutch-language fieldwork and the VOG requirement are explicit recruitment conditions.
Academic preparationMSc in a relevant social science, including public or business administration.
Research skillsQualitative methods, critical analysis and the ability to develop an independent empirical research project.
LanguageFluent Dutch and C1-level English are required.

Application dates

Recruitment dates and location

Recruitment statusSee the official vacancy for the current status
Deadline2 November 2026

LocationWageningen, Netherlands

Contact

Questions about this position, eligibility or the application process should be raised through the contact channel given on the official announcement page (see the Official Link section above). Always quote the position reference in your message so the admissions or HR team can route your enquiry quickly.

Important Notes

  • Application deadline: 2 November 2026 - late or incomplete applications are normally not considered.
  • Listing details were recorded from the official source at the time of publication; always confirm the latest requirements on the official page before applying.
  • Prepare the documents listed in the eligibility and application sections before starting the online form - transcripts, CV and references take the longest to collect.

How to Apply

  • CV: maximum two pages.
  • Motivation letter: maximum one page; keep the initial submission within three pages.

Submit through the application system linked from the official vacancy. Follow its current document and translation instructions.

Selection and Contact

Interviews are planned for 20 November 2026. The selected applicant must provide a certificate of conduct (VOG).

Research contact: Jori Kalkman; supervisory team includes Bram Büscher and Esther van ’t Veen.

About Wageningen University & Research

Wageningen University & Research works across food, agriculture, environment and society. The vacancy identifies the specific chair group and supervisory team responsible for this project.
